ledger.claim: POL-RD-01 is satisfied on both establishment gates. The governing actual distance is the trace length of 7.89 km against a booked optimal of 6.2 km, an excess of 1.69 km. That is 27.26% of the optimal distance, above the 20% gate, and 1.69 km in absolute terms, above the 0.8 km gate. Both tests pass, so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence.

The threshold test must be run on the trace figure, not the rounded copy. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 7.89 km while trip_record.actual_distance_km is 7.9 km, and POL-RD-01 provides that where the two disagree the trace governs and the trip-record figure may not be cited for the threshold test. The 1.69 km excess is measured from the trace.

The trace is clean for policy purposes and the rider does not need corroboration beyond it. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. EV-GPS-00518 shows 121 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100.0% coverage, an empty gaps array and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds. None of limbs (a) to (c) is met, so the deviation stands on the gps_trace alone.

The driver's excuse that the road 'avoids two junctions' and is 'a real shortcut when the main road is busy' cannot exonerate the route. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory that names a road, expressway segment or junction the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the time the vehicle would have reached that segment. The only advisory artifact in this case, EV-ADVIS-00518-01, is MISSING: status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT ('No advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window'). The absence is itself citable and it means POL-RD-03 cannot run at all.

The rider has discharged her initial burden and the driver has not discharged his. POL-RD-08 requires her to show the artifacts describe the same trip and an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold from an unimpaired trace: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00518, the pickup/start timestamps agree (trip_record.started_at and gps_trace.first_fix_at are both 2026-09-06T08:26:40+08:00), and the 1.69 km excess passes both gates. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, and a general assertion that traffic was bad, supported by a specific artifact and a traffic_advisory ID, is exactly what he has not produced.

No rider-requested detour can be argued against the rider. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor or within three minutes of it, identifying a place or road specifically enough to act on. EV-CHAT-00518 is a chat export with message_count 0 and an empty messages array, so there is no instruction at all and no waypoint_hint for the trace to corroborate. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record.

Neither a relocation nor a pooling baseline reduces the excess. POL-RD-05 needs an amended endpoint: on EV-TRIP-00518 pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at, original_pickup, original_dropoff and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null, so there is no amendment and no re-quote to re-run POL-RD-01 against. POL-RD-12 needs vehicle_type RYDE_POOL: the vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so the matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and the booked 6.2 km optimal is the correct comparator.

The distance refund is not closed off by upfront pricing. POL-RD-11 applies only where fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is non-null. EV-FARE-00518 records fare_model METERED and quoted_fare_sgd null, so this is a metered trip and the distance-and-time refund under POL-RD-02 is available to the rider.

The refund is arithmetic and the rider asks for exactly what POL-RD-02 yields. On the fare_breakdown: charged_total is 16.13. recomputed_fare is (3.80 base + 0.75 x 6.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 10.5 optimal min) x 1.0 surge_multiplier read from EV-FARE-00518 + 0.80 platform fee = 12.19. Refund = 16.13 - 12.19 = 3.94, which rounds UP to SGD 3.95. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and it is 24.4% of charged_total, well short of the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.95.

No pass-through correction competes with or reduces the distance refund. POL-RD-09 settles ERP, tolls and surcharges separately, but here erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.0, optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.0 and airport_surcharge is 0.0 on a trip that does not originate at an airport, so there is nothing to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and no billing-integrity line to refund under POL-RD-09(4).

The charge is still live, so a PARTIAL_REFUND moves money rather than confirming a refund the rider already has. Although the rider believed the app 'refunded the difference immediately', EV-FARE-00518 records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0. Under POL-GEN-03 the present state stands only on NO_ACTION; a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.95 returns that amount against the still-charged fare.

No corroboration condition attaches to this rider. Under POL-RD-08 an excess below 30% of optimal draws an extra corroboration requirement only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer. EV-RPROF-00518 records deviation_claims_60d 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0, so the condition is nowhere near met and the claim stands on the trace.

Neither party's profile can decide this case, and the rider does not overreach by claiming a penalty uplift. POL-RD-06 is engaged on a MATERIAL deviation or finely balanced evidence: the deviation here is 27.26% and 1.69 km, both well below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality thresholds, so it is not material; and on the driver's own profile the pattern tests fail outright, deviation_flags_90d being 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither the 3-flag test nor the 5% test is met. POL-GEN-01 confines every other profile field to context only. The rider's entitlement is therefore the POL-RD-02 partial and nothing rests on reputation.

The record does document that the driver contacted the rider after the trip: EV-TRIP-00518 carries an in_app_call placed by DRIVER at 2026-09-06T10:28:40+08:00, answered, lasting 190 seconds, more than an hour and a half after ended_at 08:46:40, and the driver's own account confirms he called to argue the fare. The rider's concern about being contacted is therefore grounded in the record, but this category's policy provides no monetary remedy for post-trip contact, and the only conduct mechanism, the POL-RD-06(c) referral, requires an established repeat pattern which the driver's clean deviation record does not supply. The rider's monetary entitlement accordingly stands on the POL-RD-02 arithmetic.

On the platform's own arithmetic this is a deviation, but a minor one: the governing trace distance is 7.89 km against a 6.2 km optimal route, an excess of 1.69 km or 27.26%. That clears POL-RD-01's 0.8 km and 20% establishment gates, but it sits under both materiality thresholds - 50% of optimal and 8.0 km absolute - so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and the driver_profile machinery of POL-RD-06 is never switched on.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern on which to hang an uplift or a referral. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in the last 90 days, so neither limb of POL-RD-06's pattern test - 3 or more flags, or a flag rate of 5% or more - is satisfied. The clause names the trailing-90-day counter and not the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter, and on the field the clause actually names the answer is zero. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral is available.

ledger.claim: Whatever the rider believes is at stake, the money is fixed by POL-RD-02 and is small: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 6.2 + 0.28 x 10.5) x 1.0) + 0.80 = 12.19, so the refund is 16.13 - 12.19 = 3.94, rounded up to 3.95, which is only 24.4% of the charged total and nowhere near the 90% share that would license a FULL_REFUND. The surge multiplier required by the formula is the 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown, so nothing inflates the recomputation.

The rider's real grievance - that the driver telephoned her after the trip and that she cannot see how he had her number - carries no monetary remedy in this category. The only conduct mechanism the deviation policy supplies is the POL-RD-06(c) referral for a repeat pattern, which is not established, and the call was in any event placed through the platform's own in-app calling channel (trip_record.in_app_calls: placed_by DRIVER, answered, 190 seconds), so the driver neither obtained nor used any personal telephone number of the rider.

The rider's account that she asked why and the driver did not answer is unsupported on this record: the trip's chat log contains zero messages, so there is no in-app exchange the driver failed to answer, and that part of her account rests on no evidence ID and carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

The rider's statement that 'the app refunded the difference immediately' is contradicted by the platform's own ledger: fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd is 0.0 and payment_status is CHARGED. Nothing has been refunded, the disputed figure of 16.13 is the whole fare, and the most this record can move is the 3.95 computed above.

Nothing is added by the pass-through lines: the fare breakdown lists no ERP gantries, tolls_erp is 0.0, and the trip did not originate at an airport, so POL-RD-09 supplies no off-route ERP or surcharge correction on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

The evidence that decides this case is clean, so the excess must be measured on the trace at the 1.69 km it actually records and the exposure stays capped at the arithmetic figure: the trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100% coverage, no gaps and a 10 second cadence, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07, no POL-GEN-02 discount applies, and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the fare for trip TRP-00518 is reduced by SGD 3.95. The rest of the charge stands.

ROUTE. The platform's own GPS trace, EV-GPS-00518, records 7.89 km driven (trace_distance_km, the figure POL-RD-01 says governs over the rounded 7.9 km trip-record copy). The booked optimal on EV-TRIP-00518 is 6.2 km. The excess is 1.69 km, which is 27.3% of optimal. Both of POL-RD-01's establishment gates are passed (more than 20%, and more than 0.8 km), so the deviation IS established. It is not a MATERIAL deviation: 27.3% is under 50% and 1.69 km is under 8.0 km, so the POL-RD-06 pattern machinery is not switched on.

FARE. This was a METERED trip (EV-FARE-00518; quoted_fare_sgd is null), so POL-RD-02 runs. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 6.2 km + 0.28 x 10.5 min) x 1.0 surge, read from the fare breakdown EV-FARE-00518, + 0.80 platform fee = 12.19, with no ERP, toll, surcharge, waiting or promo lines to add. charged_total is 16.13. Refund = 16.13 - 12.19 = 3.94, rounded up to SGD 3.95. That is above the 0.50 de minimis, and at 24.4% of the fare it is far short of the 90% share that would make it a full refund.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. The driver's account that the road avoids two junctions and is a real shortcut when the main road is busy does not reduce the refund. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses; the only advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00518-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, BLOCKING). The absence is citable, and it means POL-RD-03 cannot run. A general assertion that traffic was bad, with no advisory behind it, does not discharge the driver's burden under POL-RD-08.

THE POST-TRIP CALL. The record shows a 190-second call placed by the driver at 10:28:40 through the platform's own in-app calling channel (EV-TRIP-00518, in_app_calls - placed_by DRIVER, answered). That answers the rider's concern about how the driver had her number: it was an in-app call, not a personal telephone number. No clause in this category provides a monetary remedy for post-trip contact, and the only conduct mechanism, the POL-RD-06(c) referral, requires an established repeat-deviation pattern, which the driver's record does not show (deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days). The rider's account that she asked why and was not answered in chat is not supported by the record: the chat log EV-CHAT-00518 contains zero messages.

STATE OF THE CHARGE. Nothing has been refunded yet - the ledger shows refund_issued_sgd 0.0 and payment_status CHARGED - so the 3.95 is a fresh refund against the still-charged fare, not a confirmation of a refund already made.

CONFIDENCE. The excess is carried by the GPS trace and trip record, and the fare by the ledger, all at full weight 1.0; the missing advisory carries no fact, so confidence is 0.9.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
